text:
Gabriel Vilardi apologized for his slow start, TSN reported this week, during a stretch in which the Jets went eight games without a win. He has 1 goal in 17 games. We'd tell him to save the apology. That goal came on 5.26 expected goals of his own, a 3.2 percent shooting rate for a player who scores around the league average most years. Winnipeg has also scored 6.1 fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice.

The chances are the reassuring part. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.4 scoring chances per 60 minutes from the home-plate area in front of the net last season, the 99th percentile. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.4 wins, 34th among forwards. That player did not disappear over one bad month.

TSN also reported that Scott Arniel put him back with Kyle Connor and Mark Scheifele to spark the offense, and the Jets won the two games since. If you're looking for a player due a run, this is the clearest one on our board.
headline: Vilardi's one goal is the unluckiest number in Winnipeg
